topics.title: LTI Systems and Convolution
topics.syllabus: LTI systems: definition and properties, causality, stability, impulse response, convolution, poles and zeroes, frequency response, group delay, phase delay.

cards.title: Testing linearity, causality, time-invariance
cards.bodyHtml: Test each property separately and mechanically. For time invariance, compare the output of a delayed input against the delayed output — if the time axis is warped rather than shifted, the system is time varying.

cards.title: Poles, stability and ROC
cards.bodyHtml: Stability is a statement about where the region of convergence lies, not just about pole positions. For a causal system the ROC is outside the outermost pole; stability then needs every pole inside the unit circle.

cards.title: Frequency response, group and phase delay
cards.bodyHtml: A sinusoid into an LTI system comes out as the same sinusoid scaled by ∣H(jω)∣|H(j\omega)|∣H(jω)∣ and shifted by ∠H(jω)\angle H(j\omega)∠H(jω) — nothing else. Distortionless transmission therefore needs flat magnitude and phase linear in ω\omegaω; a constant phase is not good enough.
cards.pitfallHtml: Group delay is the delay of the envelope, phase delay that of the carrier. They are equal only when the phase is linear through the origin — a constant phase offset makes them differ.

cards.title: Impulse response and step response
cards.bodyHtml: The impulse response h(t)h(t)h(t) is the system — every property in this topic is a statement about it. The step response is its running integral, which is why a question giving one and asking for the other is a single differentiation or integration.
cards.pitfallHtml: 1/t1/t1/t decays to zero and is still not absolutely integrable, so decaying is not the same as stable. Check the integral, not the tail.

cards.title: Symmetry shortcuts
cards.bodyHtml: A real even signal has a real even transform; a real odd signal has a purely imaginary odd transform. This alone eliminates half the options in many questions.

cards.bodyHtml: Sample above twice the highest frequency or components fold back. An aliased tone appears at the distance to the nearest multiple of fsf_sfs​.
cards.pitfallHtml: Two different input tones can produce identical samples — that is exactly what aliasing means.

cards.title: Discrete-time processing of continuous-time signals
cards.bodyHtml: Sampling maps the analogue frequency Ω\OmegaΩ to the digital frequency ω=ΩT\omega=\Omega Tω=ΩT, so a digital filter acting at ω\omegaω behaves on the original signal as one at ω/T\omega/Tω/T. Decimation and interpolation each need a filter, and each for a different reason: one to prevent aliasing, the other to remove images.
cards.pitfallHtml: Order matters and is not symmetric: the anti-alias filter comes before decimation, the anti-imaging filter after interpolation. Swapping either one destroys the signal.

cards.title: DFT properties
cards.bodyHtml: The DFT is periodic and circular: shifts wrap around, and multiplication in one domain is circular convolution in the other. Applying the DFT four times returns the original scaled by N2N^{2}N2.

cards.bodyHtml: The algebra is the easy part; the ROC carries the information about causality and stability. Same expression, different ROC, different signal.
